{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)  
**Re:** Playbook review of licence, hosting and revenue-share agreement  

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Eleven clauses are compliant, five are deviations and two rules are unsatisfied because no usable clause exists.

The commercial core is favourable to us. Commerce One's IP indemnity (§ 8) is uncapped by operation of § 9 and exceeds our fallback; the audit right in § 4.4 tracks our preferred position (annual cap, independent CPA, vendor-borne costs, 5% shortfall trigger); assignment (§ 14.1) is mutual with an M&A carve-out and no change-of-control trigger; and the Agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitment, non-solicit or liquidated damages on us. Renewal is annual with a 30-day exit, and California law with a San Francisco AAA seat sits at our fallback.

Our exposure is concentrated in five areas. First, the § 9 liability cap is measured by amounts "actually paid by Corio for the transaction which the liability relates to" — a per-transaction slice that can fall below our fallback, with only § 8 carved out (confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud all remain capped). Second, the § 13.5 Developments carve-out assigns to Commerce One ownership of work we create and fund wherever it supports that work on an ongoing basis, with no licence back. Third, we have no termination-for-convenience right in a five-year initial term. Fourth, there is no exit/transition or data-return clause. Fifth, there is no vendor insurance covenant at all, despite Commerce One personnel touching our hosted environment and data. The § 7.3 warranty is substantively sound but runs only 60 days from the Effective Date with a hard 31 December 1999 cut-off, which can expire at or before acceptance under § 3.1.

We also flag a process point: five of our proposed redlines did not pass automated verification (see column below) and must be re-drafted and placed manually before the mark-up is issued.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note | Redline verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 | Full defend-and-indemnify for IP infringement with standard procedure and remedy ladder; uncapped via § 9 carve-out. Exceeds fallback. | Pass |
| High | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 (7.3–7.4) | Remedies adequate; duration fails — 60 days from Effective Date with 31 Dec 1999 cut-off may lapse at or before acceptance under § 3.1. | Repaired |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 14.1 | Mutual assignment with M&A carve-out; no change-of-control or re-pricing trigger anywhere. At/above fallback. | Pass |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation) | No sole-source or requirements obligation; Exhibit D commitments expressly non-binding. Preferred position met. | Pass |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 4 | No LDs, penalties, early-termination fee or minimum payment; § 4.2 true-up is cost recovery. | Pass |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 (Grant of Rights) | Only licence-scope limits; § 13.6 preserves independent development. Preferred position met. | Pass |
| Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13.5 | Baseline Corio ownership of Developments is correct, but the carve-out assigns our funded IP to Commerce One with no licence back — walk-away territory. | **Fail** |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 | No transition clause; Confidential Information may be "returned or destroyed" at the holder's election, with no window, format or certification. | **Fail** |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4.4 | Annual cap, independent CPA, vendor-borne cost, 5% trigger, records only. "Reasonable notice" rather than fixed period noted only. | Pass |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 | California law, San Francisco AAA arbitration — at fallback; domestic seat, no walk-away trigger. | Pass |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations on Customer | Compliant | § 4 / Exhibit B | No price-parity or matching obligation on us. Preferred position met. | Pass |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume limits | Compliant | Exhibit B (Revenue Sharing Fees) | Pure revenue share with no floor; maintenance spend is elective; Exhibit D targets non-binding. | Pass |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14 | No hiring restriction anywhere in the Agreement. Benefits us. | Pass |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 11.1 | One-year renewals, 30-day either-party non-renewal notice; Exhibit B fixes Year 2–5 pricing. | Pass |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 9 | Cap measured per transaction actually paid, below fallback; confidentiality (§ 10), gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud remain capped. | **Fail** |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 | No Customer convenience right in a five-year initial term; exits limited to non-renewal, material breach and insolvency. | **Fail** |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 (2.2) | Perpetual, irrevocable and assignable on M&A, but no affiliate or contractor coverage; § 2.2 limited to "Corio's internal business operations". | **Fail** |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 | No insurance covenant; Commerce One personnel touch our hosted environment and data. | Repaired |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away, and we should not sign without movement on them:

1. **§ 13.5 Developments carve-out (IP).** Assignment of IP we create and fund to Commerce One with no licence back to exploit it. Ask: delete the carve-out; Commerce One's background IP remains protected by the opening proviso and § 2.8.
2. **§ 11 — no Customer termination for convenience (T4C).** Absence of any convenience right across a five-year initial term. Ask: 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees (fallback: 60 days). Commerce One should remain without a mid-term convenience right.
3. **No vendor insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** No coverage obligation for a vendor with access to our data. Ask: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request (fallback: E&O 1M / cyber 2M).
4. **§ 9 liability cap (LOL-CAP).** The per-transaction basis can fall below our fallback and leaves Commerce One's own exposure at walk-away level. Ask: greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with § 10 confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud uncapped.
5. **No exit/transition or data-return clause (TRANSITION).** The "return or destroy" election edges toward the no-data-return walk-away case. Ask: new § 11.4 — six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion, expressly without limiting our surviving § 11.3 rights (fallback: 90 days' assistance).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-draft the five unverified redlines** (IP § 13.5, TRANSITION new § 11.4, LOL-CAP § 9, T4C new § 11.4, LICENSE § 2.2) and confirm placement and clause numbering manually. Note that the TRANSITION and T4C proposals both target a new § 11.4 — we will consolidate or renumber before issue.
2. **Confirm the two repaired redlines** (WARRANTY § 7.3 and the new insurance covenant in § 14) read correctly in context; numbering of the insurance clause can be conformed on execution.
3. **Issue the mark-up with our positions and fallbacks stated**: warranty 12 months from acceptance with the fixed 1999 expiry deleted (fallback 90 days from acceptance, plus a professional-and-workmanlike Services warranty with a 90-day period); liability cap and carve-outs as above; convenience termination at 30 days (fallback 60); transition assistance at six months (fallback 90 days); insurance at preferred limits (fallback E&O 1M / cyber 2M).
4. **Sequence the negotiation** around the five walk-away items first; the warranty duration and affiliate/contractor licence scope can be traded if needed.
5. **Confirm the commercial assumption** behind the warranty timing — because Acceptance Testing may itself run to 31 December 1999 under § 3.1, we should establish with the business whether acceptance is expected before that date.
6. **No action** on the eleven compliant rules. We note for the record that GOVLAW and ASSIGN sit at the fallback and are accepted as drafted, and that AUDIT, EXCLUSIVITY, LD, NONCOMPETE, MFN, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT and RENEWAL meet the preferred position.
"}
